svg.text: The one-minute claim: a new board without typing a key
Concepts 8 and 10 · a single-use claim code exchanged for a device key · the life cycle up to Deactivate
the server only keeps its SHA-256
Broker address → NVS (the Pi gateway's IP)
then Save; without the portal: Serial claim
register the device → mark the code
the 43-character key to NVS, never printed
logs in to the broker with its new key
name and location from the code
The server's answers to a claim
the 403 wording: claim code wrong, expired, or already used: ask the admin for a new code
registered: the key + the broker account already made by the server
code wrong, expired, or already used (one answer for all three)
that device is still registered and active: deactivate it first, then claim again
more than 10 attempts per minute from one IP address
a server or broker problem: the code is NOT used up; the board sends at most 3 times, 30 seconds apart
One minute = the target for a real board + phone; not measured by the author (lab: simulator, the card Online 1.7.0 3.8–6.7 seconds after starting)
The life cycle of a device
Concept 10: a lost or stolen device
a new key from the admin
the broker deletes its account: the board is disconnected at once (administrative action)
the server writes the status offline (no will is published when the account is deleted)
the key revoked, the retained config deleted; commands and updates → 409
lab: 200 within 0.18 seconds (simulator, a simulated TLS bridge)
a real board: not tested by the author
the old retained online status stays at the broker
Grafana sends a false "… is sending data again."
±4.5 minutes later (lab): set a silence before Deactivate
the key in a stolen board's NVS is still readable
(flash encryption: the Module 21 Technical Deep Dive)
